title: Real-Time Delivery & Extreme Fan-Out
summary: Choose between polling, SSE, and WebSockets, and scale live delivery across gateway fleets.
body:
Whenever clients need sub-second updates—chat messages, collaborative edits, live reactions, or seat-map drops—pick the simplest transport that matches the directionality and frequency of traffic.

## Transport selection
- Short polling (`every 5-30s`): simplest stateless HTTP; fine for coarse status checks, wasteful for instant updates.
- Long polling: server holds HTTP request open until data arrives or timeout; good fallback for infrequent notifications.
- Server-Sent Events (`SSE`): unidirectional server-to-client stream over standard HTTP; ideal for live dashboards, seat availability updates, and AI token or feed streams.
- WebSockets: full-duplex persistent TCP channel; choose when clients also send high-frequency upstream events (chat, collaborative cursors, multiplayer).

## Routing across stateful gateways
Once connections span dozens of gateway hosts, the sender's server is rarely the recipient's server:
- User-addressed (`1:1` chat, file sync): maintain a session registry or consistent-hashed pub/sub channel mapping `user_id` or `document_id` to owning gateway nodes.
- Room or broadcast (`1` stream to `5M` viewers): build a hierarchical pub/sub relay tree (`origin topic -> regional relays -> edge gateways`) so each edge host receives a message once and fans it out across local sockets in memory.

## Taming celebrity and burst skew
- Hybrid feed fan-out: push post IDs to followers' caches on write for normal accounts, but merge posts from mega-accounts on read.
- Reaction aggregation: coalesce `200,000` emoji taps/s into `1-second` count windows at the edge instead of forwarding every tap.
